competencies.title: ARC and object lifetime
competencies.summary: Can explain how ARC decides when an object is deallocated and reason about ownership.
coverageTopics: retain/release inserted at compile time, not garbage collection
why ARC applies to classes and not structs
autorelease behaviour at a working level
mistakes: believing ARC runs periodically rather than deterministically

competencies.title: Closures and capture
competencies.summary: Can explain closure capture semantics and capture lists, and predict what a closure keeps alive.
coverageTopics: closures capture by reference by default
what a stored closure keeps alive
mistakes: assuming a capture list copies the whole object graph
believing value types captured in a closure are always copied at call time

competencies.title: Escaping vs non-escaping closures
competencies.summary: Can explain what @escaping means, why the compiler cares, and its ownership implications.
coverageTopics: escaping means the closure outlives the function call
non-escaping is the default and enables optimisations
stored closures and completion handlers are escaping
mistakes: assuming non-escaping closures can be stored for later

competencies.title: weak, unowned, and retain cycles
competencies.summary: Can identify a retain cycle, choose correctly between weak and unowned, and explain what breaks when the choice is wrong.
coverageTopics: unowned: non-optional, crashes if accessed after deallocation
choosing based on lifetime guarantees, not on convenience
mistakes: using unowned to avoid optionality without a lifetime guarantee
adding [weak self] everywhere reflexively, including where no cycle exists
believing structs can participate in retain cycles directly
